correctness.rationale: The Frobenius brackets vanish at all rational points. Differentiating them at a rational point gives four cyclic bilinear gradient equations. If X3 were zero, the first and second equations would force X1=X2=0 and the fourth would force bX0²=0; if X3 is nonzero, X2 X1=X3² and X1 X0=X2² give the other nonzero coordinates. Normalize X3=1: the gradient vanishes exactly at (t⁻³,t,t⁻¹,1) for b=t⁵−t³; the fourth equation follows from the first three. The degree-two Taylor term is the product of the linear coefficient variations and the linear parts of the Frobenius brackets, since q≥3. The displayed Hessian has determinant 6b/t²−2t³=2t(2t²−3); at its zeros, 3t⁻² is a nonzero two-by-two minor. Odd characteristic gives the ordinary-node criterion. At an exceptional point, (1,t²,1/2) annihilates the Hessian, so the rational line restriction has multiplicity at least three there plus q other distinct zeros, exceeding its degree q+2. The incidence count removes exactly t=±1; the roots of 2t²=3, if nonzero and present, give distinct b=3t/4. Characteristic three has none. Replay: from /workspace, python3 reproductions/algebra.py surfaces. The independent run exhausted the rational gradient incidence sets over F3, F5, F19, F9 and F25 (0, 2, 16, 6 and 22), and checked the formal polynomial restriction on every exceptional line in those fields (0, 2, 2, 0 and 2). The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; its evaluations at rational line points alone cannot detect geometric containment, since all rational points lie on the surface. The uniform proof establishes containment and the rational census; neither the proof nor the run classifies nonrational singularities or the exceptional analytic germs.

value.rationale: The original family was constructed to study rational smoothness of space-filling surfaces. At parameters where rational smoothness fails, a sharp second-order criterion separates ordinary nodes from exceptional points and identifies a geometrically contained line, uniform over all odd finite fields. This information is not recoverable from a rational-point count alone and gives concrete local geometry for the known family without overstating what happens over the algebraic closure.
